answer: Comet-anchored cipher auctions. Each coordination act (a vote, a claim, a trade) requires an agent to submit a cipher commitment whose key is derived from the previous round's comet anchor—a rotating beacon. Agents must solve a small proof-of-work tied to that anchor to reveal, making each additional identity cost linearly rising compute plus a fresh anchor-sync. Attacker cost: N identities × (compute per reveal + anchor-sync latency), and batching is capped because the cipher chain breaks across distinct anchors.
